cpr.title: CPR — Adult
cpr.warning: Call 193 FIRST. Only perform CPR if the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.

steps.instruction: Check the scene is safe, then check the person. Tap their shoulders firmly and shout "Are you okay?"
Call 193 (National Ambulance) immediately or ask a bystander to call. Put on speaker.
Lay the person on their back on a firm, flat surface. Tilt head back gently and lift chin to open the airway.
Check for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds. Look for chest rise, listen, and feel for breath.
steps.tip: Occasional gasps are NOT normal breathing — begin CPR.

steps.instruction: Place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest (lower half of breastbone). Place other hand on top, interlock fingers, and keep arms straight.
Push hard and fast — compress at least 5 cm (2 inches) deep at 100–120 compressions per minute.
steps.tip: Think of the beat of "Stayin' Alive" — that's the right pace.

steps.instruction: After 30 compressions, give 2 rescue breaths: pinch the nose, seal mouth over theirs, breathe until chest rises. Continue 30:2 cycle until help arrives.
steps.tip: If uncomfortable with rescue breaths, continuous chest compressions alone are still effective.

choking.title: Choking — Heimlich
choking.warning: If the person can still cough forcefully, encourage them to keep coughing. Only intervene if they cannot cough, speak, or breathe.

steps.instruction: Ask clearly "Are you choking?" If they cannot speak, cough, or breathe — act immediately.
Stand behind them, lean them forward slightly, and give up to 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Check mouth after each blow.
If back blows do not work, stand behind them and wrap your arms around their waist.
Make a fist with one hand and place it — thumb side in — just above the belly button, well below the breastbone.
Grasp your fist with your other hand. Pull sharply inward and upward — up to 5 times.
steps.tip: Each thrust must be a sharp, distinct movement aimed to dislodge the blockage.

steps.instruction: Alternate 5 back blows with 5 abdominal thrusts until the object clears or the person becomes unconscious.
If they become unconscious, lower them carefully to the floor and start CPR. Call 193 immediately.

bleeding.title: Severe Bleeding
bleeding.warning: Call 193 for severe or uncontrolled bleeding. Do NOT remove objects embedded in a wound.

steps.instruction: Protect yourself — use gloves if available, otherwise a plastic bag or thick cloth as a barrier.
Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth, dressing, or clothing. Press hard and hold continuously.
Do NOT lift the cloth to check — this disrupts clotting. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top and press harder.
steps.tip: Maintain pressure for at least 10–15 minutes without releasing.

steps.instruction: If the wound is on a limb and bleeding is life-threatening, apply a tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound. Tighten until bleeding stops. Write down the time applied.
Keep the person still and warm. Lay them down and raise their legs (unless head/neck injury suspected) to reduce shock risk.

burns.title: Burns Treatment
burns.warning: Call 193 for burns larger than the person's palm, burns on face/hands/genitals, or any chemical/electrical burn.

steps.instruction: Remove the person from danger. For chemical burns, brush off dry chemicals first before removing clothing (cut if necessary, do not pull over head).
Cool the burn under cool (not cold or iced) running water for at least 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Start within 3 hours. This single step reduces tissue damage more than anything else.

steps.instruction: While cooling, remove jewellery, watches, and clothing near the burn — but NOT if stuck to the skin.
Do NOT apply butter, toothpaste, oil, ice, or any home remedies. Do NOT burst blisters.
Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy material — cling film (plastic wrap) is ideal. Layer it rather than wrapping tightly.
Keep the person warm with a blanket (avoiding the burn area) to prevent hypothermia from prolonged cooling.

seizure.title: Seizure Response
seizure.warning: Call 193 if: first seizure, lasts more than 5 minutes, they don't regain consciousness, or they are injured.

steps.instruction: Stay calm. Note the exact time the seizure started. Most seizures end on their own within 1–3 minutes.
Protect the person — cushion their head with something soft. Clear hard or sharp objects away from them.
Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements. Do NOT put anything in their mouth.
steps.tip: People cannot swallow their tongue. Putting something in the mouth is dangerous and wrong.

steps.instruction: If possible, gently turn them onto their side (recovery position) to keep the airway clear, especially if vomiting.
Stay with them until full consciousness returns. Speak calmly and reassuringly — they may be confused and frightened for several minutes after.

eye.title: Eye Injury
eye.warning: Seek immediate care for any penetrating eye injury, chemical splash, or sudden vision loss.

steps.instruction: Do NOT rub the eye — this can worsen any injury. Keep the person as still and calm as possible.
For chemical splash: immediately flush the eye with clean water for at least 15–20 minutes, holding the eyelid open. Tilt head so water runs away from the other eye.
For a foreign object: try blinking rapidly or flushing with clean water. Do NOT try to remove anything embedded in the eye.
Cover the injured eye loosely with a clean cloth — do not apply pressure. Cover both eyes for penetrating injuries to reduce movement.
Get to a hospital or eye clinic as soon as possible, even if pain seems mild initially.
Keep the injured area completely still. Do NOT try to straighten the limb. Support it in the position found using your hands or rolled clothing.
Check circulation below the injury: feel for a pulse, check skin colour, and ask if they feel tingling or numbness.
steps.tip: Pale, cold, or bluish skin below the injury means circulation is compromised — this is urgent.

steps.instruction: For an open fracture (bone visible): cover loosely with a clean cloth — do NOT press on the bone. Treat bleeding by pressing around the wound, not on it.
Splint if moving is necessary: use a rigid item (board, rolled newspaper) padded with cloth. Secure above and below the fracture — never directly over it.
Apply a cold pack (wrapped in cloth) to reduce swelling. Keep the person warm, treat for shock, and monitor until help arrives.

poisoning.title: Poisoning / Overdose
poisoning.warning: Call 193 immediately. Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically directed by medical staff — it can cause further harm.

steps.instruction: Call 193 immediately or take the person to the nearest emergency department. Give the substance name, amount, and time taken if known.
If conscious and alert, ask what they took. Save and show the container, packaging, or substance to medical staff.
Do NOT give anything to eat or drink. Do NOT induce vomiting unless explicitly told by a doctor.
If unconscious but breathing, place in the recovery position (on their side) to prevent choking on vomit.
If they stop breathing, begin CPR. Check breathing and consciousness continuously until help arrives.
For skin/eye chemical contact: remove contaminated clothing and flush the area with large amounts of clean water for at least 20 minutes.
